fi_control_19731276: OLD: The prehistory of Finland is the period preceding Finland's historical era, from which there are no written sources. The prehistoric period of Finland began when the first inhabitants came to Finland after the last ice age, around 8850 BCE. The ice age destroyed traces of possible contemporary and earlier settlement in Finland. The prehistory of Finland is divided into the Stone Age (-1500 BCE), the Bronze Age (1500 BCE - 500 BCE) and the Iron Age (500 BCE - 1200/1300 CE). It is possible, though not certain, that on the southwest coast of Finland a Proto-Indo-European language was spoken for quite a long time at the end of the Stone Age. It is also possible that speakers of many later vanished Finnic languages arrived in the territory of Finland in the Bronze Age. However, Baltic Finns or Sami had not yet arrived in the territory of Finland at that time. Researchers do not know for certain what language the inhabitants of Finland spoke before the start of the common era.
